`git worktree remove .claude/worktrees/<name>` fails on **every** lobu worktree with:

```
fatal: working trees containing submodules cannot be moved or removed
```

That is the `owletto` submodule, which `make task-setup` pins into each worktree — so it
is not an occasional case, it is all of them.

Working removal:

```sh
rm -rf ".claude/worktrees/<name>" && git worktree prune
```

`git worktree prune` (from the main checkout) reaps the stale metadata afterwards. This
does NOT delete the branch ref — commits stay reachable via `refs/heads/<branch>`, which
is what makes a bulk sweep low-risk even if one entry is misclassified.

**Budget the time.** Each worktree carries a populated `node_modules`, so `rm -rf` runs
~15–25s. A 31-worktree sweep exceeded a 10-minute foreground timeout at 22 removed —
run bulk cleanup in the background.

## Picking what is safe to remove

Do NOT classify by ancestry. `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD` reports `1` for
almost every squash-merged branch, because a squash writes a new commit with no ancestry
link (see [[reference_squash_merge_breaks_ancestry_checks]]). On a 67-worktree sweep that
misread 29 merged branches as unmerged.

Classify against real PR state instead:

```sh
gh pr list --state merged --limit 400 --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName' > /tmp/merged.txt
gh pr list --state open   --limit 200 --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName' > /tmp/open.txt
```

Remove only when the tree is clean AND the branch is in the merged list. Re-check
`git status --porcelain` immediately before each `rm -rf` rather than trusting an earlier
snapshot — worktrees go dirty on their own from build artifacts (`pi-loader-hardening`
did exactly that mid-sweep and was correctly skipped).

**SHIPPED 2026-08-05 as lobu#2522, squash `848dfcb0ebb0d709df57895768edd9d38c9a3b20`** —
config-only, 2 files (+27). Originated as an uncommitted experiment in the **main checkout**
during the reviewer-quota cascade (see [[project_audit_peek_and_liveness_merge_handoff]]).

## A provider addition should be CONFIG-ONLY — the TS entry is a trap

The experiment put `qwen: "DASHSCOPE_API_KEY"` into **`DEFAULT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL_ENV`**
(`agent-worker/src/runtime/model-resolver.ts`), a provider → **base URL** env map.
`session-runner.ts:842` does `providerBaseUrl = credentialStore.get(baseUrlEnvVar)`, so a
Qwen run would have used **the API key string as its base URL** — the secret embedded in a
malformed URL surfacing in errors and logs.

It was also **unnecessary**: `api-key-provider-module.ts:132` already derives
`baseUrlEnvVar` as `envVarName.replace("_KEY", "_BASE_URL")` → `DASHSCOPE_API_BASE_URL`, and
`registerDynamicProvider()` (`session-runner.ts:797`) installs it at startup. Worse, that
function early-returns on `if (!alreadyRegistered)`, so **a hardcoded entry WINS over the
config-derived one** and can silently drift from `providers.json`. The map is documented as a
fallback for providers *absent* from the config. Adding a provider needs **zero TypeScript**.

## The group-name contract, which only integration CI catches

`config/providers.json` group `name` must equal what `url-builder.ts:222 providerDisplayName()`
derives: `PROVIDER_DISPLAY_NAMES[slug]` if pinned, else **capitalise the slug**. The contract
test is `packages/server/src/utils/__tests__/render-agent-error.test.ts` → "matches
config/providers.json for every registered provider", and it runs in the
**integration-vitest** shard — so `pre-commit` (biome + tsc), `make review`, and every fast
gate pass while it fails. Naming the group `"Qwen / DashScope"` against slug `qwen` failed
with `expected 'Qwen returned an error:' to be 'Qwen / DashScope returned an error:'`.

Fix was to name the group `"Qwen"` — every sibling group uses a single product name
(`Groq`, `z.ai`, `OpenCode Zen`), and the vendor detail belongs in `description` /
`apiKeyInstructions`. Adding a `PROVIDER_DISPLAY_NAMES` override would have been the wrong
lever for a name that derives fine.

**`make review` did NOT catch this** (verdict 88, 0 bugs) — it ran a couple of bun tests, not
the vitest shard. A config change can still break a contract test; wait for CI.

Also fixed en route: the experiment had flipped the unrelated **OpenCode Zen** group's
`defaultModel` from `claude-sonnet-4-6` to a fabricated `qwen-2.5-coder-32b-instruct`.

## Follow-ups

- Not yet prod-verified: Qwen appearing in the provider-connect UI (merged after the
  `9224fce77` rollout). Gate on `848dfcb0e`.
- `providers-live.yml` skips the Qwen row until a `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY` repo secret exists —
  see [[project_providers_live_ci]].
- `.pi-subagents/` and `.codex/` were gitignored separately in **#2523** (`a6b9cd015`).

**1. Qwen provider — shipped as #2522** (`848dfcb0e`). You were right that it's a config change, and it turned out to be *more* config-only than the original: I dropped the `model-resolver.ts` line entirely rather than fixing it, because `api-key-provider-module.ts:132` already derives `DASHSCOPE_API_BASE_URL` from `envVarName`, and `registerDynamicProvider` early-returns on `if (!alreadyRegistered)` — so a hardcoded entry would have *won* over the config and could silently drift. Final diff: 2 files, +27, zero TypeScript.

CI caught a real bug my review missed. There's a contract test asserting every `providers.json` group name equals what `providerDisplayName()` derives (capitalised slug unless pinned). `Qwen / DashScope` vs slug `qwen` failed with `expected 'Qwen returned an error:' to be 'Qwen / DashScope returned an error:'`. I renamed the group to `Qwen` — the right fix regardless, since every sibling uses a single product name and the vendor detail already sits in `description`. Worth knowing: **that test lives in the `integration-vitest` shard**, so pre-commit, `tsc`, and `make review` (verdict 88, "0 bugs") all passed while it was broken.

On merging without review — I couldn't. `pi-review` and `ui-review` are required statuses with `enforce_admins`; GitHub rejected the merge outright. I did skip `pre-pr` and `review-fix`.

**2. Prod verification — #2509 and #2513 are verified.** The rollout had already advanced to `9224fce77` (both pods on one image, 0 restarts).

For #2513 I caught the transition live. Sampling 18 device connections twice, 30s apart: three devices advanced `last_seen` by 28–30s, while the MacBook Pro advanced by **0s** and flipped `online: true` @98s → `false` @128s, `device_status: "offline"`. That's the discrimination that matters — an ingest stall would have taken all four devices offline together; one going silent while three keep polling is genuinely offline, truthfully reported. Under the old 20-minute window that machine would have read "online" for ~18 more minutes. Healthy devices poll every ~30s, so 4x headroom under the 120s window — no flapping risk.

For #2509, `knowledge.read` with one content_id *and* with three (the list shape) both return `request_status: "complete"`. The strip is gone, which is the entire change.

Two things I did **not** verify, to be straight about it: the non-author gating on `request`/`request_bytes` — I'm authenticated as workspace owner, so I can't observe the denied case; it rests on the integration test. And #2513's timeout *reason string* naming the age — no run dispatched to the offline device, so that text was never produced in prod, and forcing it would mean a prod write.

**3. The directories** — `.pi-subagents/` (1.3 MB) is pi subagent transcripts and prompts; `.codex/` (116 KB) is Codex-generated HTML visualizations from the social-interest radar work. Both gitignored in **#2523** (`a6b9cd015`), as a separate PR since it's a distinct concern. They still show untracked in your main checkout only because it sits on `feat/behavior-executors`, which predates that merge.

**4.** #2522 hasn't rolled out yet (merged minutes ago). A self-rescheduling wakeup is set for ~25 min carrying the gate — pod-image check rather than a `/health` probe, ancestry test in merge-commit-first order — plus a regression check that OpenCode Zen's `defaultModel` is still `claude-sonnet-4-6`. It writes its own closure line to memory and stops.

Confidence:
- **#2513 prod behavior — 97%.** Observed the actual online→offline transition with a control group of three devices still polling. Only the reason-string wording is unverified.
- **#2509 prod behavior — 88%.** Verified the server contract on both read shapes; the non-author denial is inferred from tests, not observed, and I didn't load the Activity UI.
- **#2522 correctness — 92%.** Full CI green including the shard that caught the bug, plus the contract test run locally 13/13. Not 100% until it's live in the catalog.
- **#2523 — 99%.** Ignore-only; verified zero tracked files match either pattern.

Worth your attention: `git worktree prune` would not reap the qwen worktree even with `--expire now` (the `modules/` submodule metadata blocks it) — I had to `rm -rf .git/worktrees/<name>`. That's a sharper version of the workaround already in your notes, and it'll bite any future cleanup sweep.
